comparator.name: Pedagogical Sciences (Pedagogische wetenschappen)
comparator.academicYear: Current UU published bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-28
comparator.sourceNotes: The official curriculum describes a three-year bachelor. Its first year contains eight named block courses, and the coherent pathway assigns the standard 7.5 EC to each. The second year likewise uses eight 7.5-EC block slots; where block four presents Pedagogische Praktijkontwikkeling, onderzoek en beleid and Doing a qualitative research project as alternatives beside Test- en observatievaardigheden, the first-listed option is selected by official order. The official page states that one quarter of the degree is genuine profiling space, giving 45 EC, and places the thesis across the final two blocks; the thesis is recorded as 15 EC. The pathway therefore totals 120 EC in years one and two, a 15-EC thesis and 45 EC of open profiling space. No particular profiling elective, minor, stage or study-abroad option is invented.

alternatives.label: Child development in family, school & society
alternatives.concept: Combines developmental and social psychology, cognition, family and school contexts, sociology, communication, ethics and empirical methods to study children and adolescents in the environments where they grow up. It is the closest feasible UCR response, while UCR lacks dedicated pedagogy, family-support practice, diagnostics and supervised clinical training.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed plan balances developmental psychology with family, school, peer and wider social contexts plus communication and research.
progression: Psychology, sociology, philosophy and communication foundations precede advanced development, assessment, cognition, social theory and research. All prerequisites and offerings pass; ten 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Developmental difficulties, mental health & youth support
alternatives.concept: Develops Utrecht's developmental-difficulties and youth-support evidence through developmental psychology, psychopathology, psychodiagnostics, health psychology, neuroscience, biology, resilience and research methods. It does not claim to reproduce specialist pedagogical qualification, diagnostics or supervised practice.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum gives sustained weight to developmental risk, mental health, assessment, biological context and evidence-based support.
alternatives.distinctness: Relative to the closest plan, this route replaces much of the sociology, communication and philosophy strand with biomedical foundations, public health, life science, ecology and advanced clinical-developmental psychology. Eleven courses differ, so the educational choice is substantially more health- and intervention-oriented.
progression: Brain, behaviour, biology and psychology foundations precede advanced clinical, developmental, biomedical and research courses. Formal prerequisites and offerings pass; eleven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Children, families & social policy
alternatives.concept: Uses Utrecht's societal-pedagogy and youth-policy evidence to organise sociology, political institutions, law, economic policy, gender history, inclusion and resilience around how society supports children and families.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed plan centres social structures, public institutions, inequality, rights and policy responses affecting children, families and young people.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces most developmental, cognitive and clinical psychology courses with law, political science, public economics, social theory, gender history and policy. It differs from both earlier plans by well over 30 EC and treats child development principally through institutions and social conditions.
progression: Introductory sociology, politics, law, economics and methods precede advanced rights, public policy, social theory and resilience work. All prerequisites and offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

candidates.label: Developmental difficulties, mental health & youth support

selection.assessment: The family-school-society plan is the closest feasible UCR response. The programme's direct evidence for developmental difficulties and for societal youth policy also supports distinct health/intervention and social-policy directions. All three are coherent, feasible and pairwise differ by more than 30 EC, so production stops at three.

notes.text: Utrecht's programme is a dedicated Pedagogical Sciences degree with compulsory child-development pedagogy, diagnostics, intervention, professional communication, testing and observation, policy-oriented practice and a thesis. UCR can build strong developmental, psychological, social, ethical, policy and research foundations, but it does not reproduce the profession-specific pedagogical and supervised clinical-skills sequence.
